messages:
maria: quick check — proposal: move retry/backoff for paginated unary page fetches into the transport layer, and keep the SDK iterator logic minimal. tradeoffs?

kevin: hmm i like keeping iterator ergonomics small, but surface needs control over idempotency. if transport silently retries a page fetch we risk re-running non-idempotent server ops.

ali: runtime perspective: if transport exposes a resume-token handshake we can make retries safe. transport can re-issue FetchPage(cursor) with same nonce/header so server can dedupe.

sophie: docs concern — cross-lang UX must be consistent. Python generator vs TS async-iterator vs Go channel should behave the same w.r.t. duplicates and final error semantics.

ci-bot: test-suite: flaky test in pagination-integration on windows, left logs at https://ci.internal/runs/5421 :eyeglasses:

kevin: concrete TS example for clarity: \n\n```\n// TS\nfor await (const page of client.listWidgets({ project })) {\n  for (const w of page.items) process(w)\n}\n```\n\nkevin: If transport retries internally, does server return overlapping results? that's why resume-token needs to be first-class.

maria: proposal v1: transport exposes safeRetry(fn, { idempotent: bool, resumeToken?: string }) and SDK iterator calls transport.fetchPage(cursor) wrapped in safeRetry. transport attaches request-nonce and respects resumeToken headers.

ali: proto-level shape: FetchPage(Request { cursor }) returns Page { items, next_cursor } — transport will add header x-request-nonce and x-resume-token (if present). Server side can treat nonce+cursor as dedupe key. we'll implement header hooks in runtime.

kevin: alternative is surface-level retry: iterator itself implements retries and backoff so transport stays dumb. pros: clearer idempotency control per-call; cons: duplication across languages, more surface complexity.

sophie: for docs, we could expose three modes: "transport" (default for unary page fetches), "surface" (user-managed), "none". show opt-out example.

maria: streaming endpoints are different — for streaming list/subscribe we should not retry automatically because re-establishing streams has stronger ordering/dup semantics. surface should handle reconnection + resume for streams.

ali: agreed. runtime will treat streaming RPCs as reconnect+resume-capable but won't attempt automatic fetch-level retries.

kevin: tests we need:\n- simulate transient network fail after N pages, ensure iterator resumes from last next_cursor and no duplicates\n- ensure when user callback performs side-effects, transport-level retries don't silently replay those side-effects

maria: also decide on final error shape: iterator should raise a single consistent exception type across languages, with cause + last_known_resume_token in metadata so caller can resume manually if desired.

sophie: small docs snippet (python): \n\n```\n# python\nfor page in client.list_items(project="x"):\n    for item in page.items:\n        handle(item)\n```\n\nsophie: and opt-out example: client.list_items(..., retry_mode="surface") so advanced users can implement custom semantics.

ali: runtime action: add header hooks x-request-nonce + x-resume-token and a minimal server-side dedupe doc.

kevin: sdk action: i will draft iterator API & config for retry_mode and backoff params for python + ts + go. will include interop tests.

maria: docs action: sophie to add examples and decision note. target RFC follow-up next Wednesday.

kevin: ack, i'll post a PR with TS + Python shapes by EOD Friday.

sophie: noted. will prepare docs scaffold.

maria: thanks everyone — let's capture this in the RFC follow-up and ensure test coverage for the dup/no-dup scenarios. :thumbsup:
